summary: Retained receipt bd84c33f4fe647bc9470b0b48f324bca (completed, exit 0) shows the same held-proposal harm is reached through joint consensus, not only through a simple removal: with a ConfChangeV2 whose transition is JointImplicit carrying remove node 3, the member applied one conf-change entry carrying the removal and its own configuration then excluded it from both halves, and after the re-add with leader 1 unchanged all seventeen comparisons are complete and satisfied, with the witness admission chain matched as context, re-admission, removal and admission (parsed indices 5, 4, 2 and 6) and the removal prerequisite recording transition joint_implicit with voter false and outgoing false. The same run reproduces the witness pending at 1201 ms with release only at the caller deadline and no committed payload, the context-free invocation pending at 2000 ms and uncommitted before being admitted and committed after the leader change, the configuration proposal pending at 800 ms with nothing applied, the never-removed member returning in 0 ms and committing, both retries pending while member proposals committed in those intervals, and the post-leader-change invocation returning in 0 ms and committing. The interpretation for experiment 6b5eedab76ea4fa7804929359921df36-experiment links all six lineage receipts by joint history, adds the joint-route fact with its indices, replaces the single-removal-form limitation with the accurate remaining boundary that transitions keeping the member in a configuration half were not executed and are expected not to disarm the gate only by source reading, and discloses that the executed revision's prefix prose still described a simple removal while the fixed harness performed the joint one.
